subject: EvoAI Dedicated Capacity Decision Kit — token-burst & tiling inventory
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alexg@evo.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-17T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: EvoAI Dedicated Capacity Decision Kit — token-burst & tiling inventory

Alex —

Thanks for the time last week. To get the Dedicated sizing scoped for EvoAI I put together a short "decision kit" we use to size reserved vs burst capacity and to map GPU tiling/slotting for multi-workload customers. Attached are two sample files (token_histogram_sample.csv, example_prompts.txt) — if you can share your equivalents we can produce a capacity sketch quickly.

What would be most helpful in the next 48–72 hours:
- A 1-week sample (CSV) with per-minute rows containing: timestamp, active_sessions, concurrent_requests, total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms. (See attached token_histogram_sample.csv for formatting.)
- A count of distinct workloads (chat, summarization, embedding, rerank) and the percent of traffic each represents.
- Peak concurrency (concurrent in-flight LLM generations) observed and the peak 5-minute sustained TPS.
- Typical session lifetime (median and 95th percentile) and how often sessions re-use a cached prefix / KV entries.
- Percentage of requests with long generated responses (>512 tokens) vs short (<64 tokens).
- SLA / p99 latency target you expect for 95% of calls (e.g., p99 <= 250ms for short completions).
- Any preferences for model family (7B vs 13B) and whether EvoAI is comfortable with quantized 4-bit variants for cost optimization.
- Procurement timeline (PO date target) and whether you need a firm committed capacity number for your internal approval.

Two clarifying notes on our side:
1) For burst-heavy profiles we usually recommend a combination of reserved capacity sized to sustained baseline + a burst pool sized to cover 90th–99th percentile windows, with automatic fallback to a smaller model when burst caps are hit.
2) If you rely heavily on prefix/KV caching (e.g., chat sessions that reuse a shared context), reserved capacity needs are often reduced substantially — please indicate an estimated cache hit rate.

If it's easier we can hop on a 30-minute intake call tomorrow — I have an opening 2028-09-18 at 10:30am PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_histogram_sample.csv (CSV example), example_prompts.txt (prompt samples)

From: Alex Gomez <alexg@evo.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Purchasing Team <procurement@evo.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-17T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EvoAI Dedicated Capacity Decision Kit — token-burst & tiling inventory

Stephanie —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a 7-day sample (we obfuscated user ids) and a small prompt set. Quick answers inline below to speed things up:

- Workloads: chat (70%), batch summarization (15%), embeddings (10%), rerank (5%).
- Peak concurrency: 1,250 concurrent generators observed; peak 5-minute sustained TPS ~ 320 generations/minute (we measure generations as a single response completion).
- Session lifetime: median = 120s, 95th = 1,100s. About 48% of sessions reuse a cached prefix (we tag session replays server-side).
- Token distribution: ~58% short (<64 tokens), ~32% medium (64–512), ~10% long (>512). Average prompt tokens = 48, average response tokens = 240.
- Latency targets: for interactive chat we aim for p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300–350ms depending on model size. For batch jobs p99 is non-critical.
- Model preference: primary is a 13B family (for quality), but we're open to 7B quantized as a fallback in severe cost windows.
- Procurement timeline: target PO by 2028-10-10. We will need a draft commitment number by 2028-09-25 for internal budget approvals.

I've uploaded two files: token_histogram_sample.csv and example_prompts.txt (attached). Let me know if you need a different aggregation window. Happy to take the 30-minute intake — 2028-09-18 10:30am PT works for me.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Head of Infrastructure
EvoAI

Attachments: token_histogram_sample.csv, example_prompts.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-18T07:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: EvoAI Dedicated Capacity Decision Kit — token-burst & tiling inventory

Stephanie —

Looping in a quick internal take after glancing at their CSV: their peak 5-min TPS vs sustained baseline looks like ~3.5x. Given the high % of short interactive requests and a 13B preference, I'd tentatively recommend we propose:

- Reserved: capacity to cover 40–50% of observed peak concurrency (conservative baseline sizing),
- Burst pool: enough to cover up to 90th percentile peak windows (auto-scale),
- Fallback model plan: 7B quantized automatic downgrade for excess burst beyond burst pool.

We should also call out median session reuse (48%) as a potential reduction lever for purchased reserved QPS. Would like to review cost delta between reserved-only vs reserved+burst scenarios before we present numbers.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alexg@evo.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Purchasing Team <procurement@evo.ai>

Subject: Re: EvoAI Dedicated Capacity Decision Kit — token-burst & tiling inventory

Alex / Team —

Great, appreciate the sample and the quick responses. Next steps:
1) Intake call: 2028-09-18 10:30am PT (confirmed). Agenda: walk the CSV column-by-column, discuss p99 targets per workload, and agree on a conservative reserved baseline number for internal approvals.
2) Deliverable by 2028-09-25: a one-page capacity decision sheet with two options (Reserved+Burst and Reserved-Only) including GPU mix, estimated monthly token cost, and fallback model plan.
3) Please confirm whether procurement will accept a 60-day delivery window for hardware-backed Dedicated start or if you require guaranteed start dates tied to a PO.

I'll bring a baseline sketch to the call; Marissa and Ben will join to cover cost modeling and topology. Linking the working doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcEvo-Capacity-Decision-Kit and HubSpot record HS-2093845.

Thanks — talk tomorrow.

—Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
